chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The perfume of women is that which displays its color and hides its smell, and the perfume of men is that which manifests its smell and hides its color.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the recommended qualities of perfume for men and women in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the distinct aesthetic ideals for gendered fragrance, where women's beauty is associated with visible elegance and subtle scent, while men's is defined by potent aroma and modest appearance. In Shia scholarly tradition, this reflects the broader concept of *fitrah* (natural disposition), guiding believers in adhering to modesty and attractiveness appropriate to their gender. It serves as a practical guideline for personal grooming, emphasizing that true beauty lies in the harmony between outward presentation and inner essence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Perfume of the women is what displays its colour and hides its smell, and a perfume of the men is what manifests its smell and hides its colour’.
en.sarwar: 17. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, “Perfume for women is that which shows its color but hides its fragrance, and the perfume for men is that which spreads its fragrance but its color does not show.’””
